title: "Confidence interval"
params:
  lang: en
---

```{r, include=FALSE}
library(exams)
library(mathml)
library(htmltools)
library(mistakes)

hook(n, N)
hook(xbar, mean(X))
hook(s_d, subscript(s, D))
hook(quant, t)
hook(mu0, subscript(mu, 0L))

task <- "confint2"
plfile <- file.path("rexams", sprintf("%s.pl", task))
rolog::consult(system.file(plfile, package="mistakes"))

source("utility.R")

## DATA GENERATION
repeat
{
  n <- as.integer(round(runif(1, min=25, max=50)))
  mu0 <- round(runif(1, 4, 7),1) 
  xbar <- mu0 + round(runif(1, 0.5, 1.5),1)
  s_d <- round(runif(1, 1.5, 2.5),1)
  Q <- quote(search(confint2, confint2(n, xbar, s_d, mu0), .S, .R, .P, .E))
  S <- findall(Q, options=list(preproc=as.rolog), env=environment())

  if(problems(S))
    next

  break
}

t <- prepare(task=task, S)
sol <- format_feedback(t$correct, t$explanations, t$bugs, t$praise, t$blame, t$extra)
```

Question
========
A sample of $N=`r n`$ university students took part in a semester-long program 
designed to improve their overall well-being. 
The researchers expected the mean well-being score at the end of the program to be higher 
than the reference value of $\mu_0=`r mu0`$ points.
At the end of the program, the students completed a questionnaire. 
Their mean score is $\overline{X}=`r xbar`$ points, and their sample variance is $s_\mathrm{D}=`r s_d`$ points. 
Assuming that well-being scores are approximately normally distributed, 
calculate the two-sided $95\%$ confidence interval. 


```{r questionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(t$alternatives, markup="markdown")
```

Solution
========
The two-sided $95\%$ confidence interval is calculated by: `r t$solution`

```{r solutionlist, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
sol <- lapply(sol, FUN=gsub, pattern="\\n", replacement="")
answerlist(sol, markup="markdown")
```
